title: AI Stock Pullback Coming? 3 Stocks Im Preparing To Buy + BE & HOOD Update (Options With Ryan)

steps.does: Opens the account overview and notes the account is near all-time highs.
steps.why: Frame the video with current account progress toward his long-term goal.
data: account near all-time highs
steps.conclusion: Account is right up near all-time highs.

steps.does: Opens the realized gain/loss page and shows the trades closed for profit that day and the total for the current month.
steps.why: Show transparency of results and that the month is on track.
data: several trades closed for profit on the day
current month realized total
steps.conclusion: Right on track for the month.

steps.does: Contrasts S&P 500 near all-time highs and VIX around 15 with the share of S&P stocks above their 50-day average on a chart; later reads the Nasdaq-100 equivalent (47% versus 52% the day before).
steps.why: To see under the hood: a weak breadth reading means concentration in mega caps rather than an overbought market, and a drop in the Nasdaq-100 reading versus S&P shows rotation.
data: 31% of S&P stocks above 50-day average, recovering from Iran-war lows
NDFI at 47% versus 52% the day before
S5FI low starting to creep up
steps.conclusion: Weak, not overbought market; rotation from AI/mega cap tech into beaten-up S&P names is likely, so tech pullbacks are the time to act.

steps.does: Opens the market tide page and reads net put/call flow by ticker and the market sentiment gauge.
steps.why: To see whether institutions are hedging or chasing and whether sentiment is fearful.
data: defensive put buying in MU, Nvidia, AMD, AVGO, Apple, QQQ
call action in Tesla, Amazon, Palantir
sentiment gauge showing fear territory
steps.conclusion: Mixed day with hedging in AI names; overall market in fear, a good time to start placing cash-secured puts for rich premiums.

rules.text: Fear-zone sentiment with higher volatility is a good time to start selling cash-secured puts for rich premiums.

steps.does: Opens the FedWatch tool and reads the probability of a rate hike at the October and December meetings, then relates it to next week's CPI release.
steps.why: To see whether further hikes are priced and what cooler inflation could change.
data: 80% odds of no change in October
98% odds for December
CPI due next Wednesday; core PPI Thursday
steps.conclusion: Fifth hike still off the table; cool CPI could push hikes out or remove one.

steps.does: On charts for QQQ, SMH, AAT, GLW, HOOD, BE and a photonics ETF, notes price relative to the mid and lower Bollinger Band, the 20/50/200-day moving averages, yearly VWAP, RSI and MACD; measures SMH's 18% run from Sept 16 to Oct 6.
steps.why: To judge whether a run is stretched and where support such as the mid-band or 50-day sits.
data: QQQ mid Bollinger Band about 737 as short-term support
SMH hugging upper Bollinger Band after 18% gain
AAT bounced off 200-day, +33% from lows, about 8% pullback
AAT RSI mid-range, MACD slowing
HOOD at lower band, bounced off 50-day, fell from 150 to low 60s
GLW just below yearly VWAP, 71 P/E versus 120 earlier
steps.conclusion: Expects more pullback in AI and mega cap tech names; uses mid band or 50-day as targets.

rules.text: A stock hugging the upper Bollinger Band after a big run normally pulls back to the mid band, possibly overshooting.

steps.does: Opens market maker/GEX data for each candidate, reads where call and put walls sit and whether support exists, and for QQQ reads the expected two-week range.
steps.why: To see whether option market makers provide support under a candidate and where upside resistance is before selling puts.
data: QQQ expected range high 771, low 727
AAT no put wall; above 512 may accelerate, resistance 535
GLW call wall 165, acceleration below 145
HOOD call wall 120
BE put wall support at 270
photonics ETF call wall at 30
steps.conclusion: BE has put wall support so this may be the pullback; AAT has no put wall support so more downside is possible.

steps.does: For each candidate, places cash-secured put strikes at or below the lower or mid Bollinger Band, the 50-day average or VWAP, and shows the strikes already layered in his account.
steps.why: Get assigned only at prices he is comfortable owning while collecting rich premium.
data: AAT puts at 500, 475, 445
GLW 135 to 140 strikes below lower band
HOOD 105 and 99 puts, maybe low 90s next
BE 240 and 225 puts, 225 near VWAP
photonics ETF around 23 strike near lower band, monthly options only
steps.conclusion: Layer puts at several strikes rather than going in at one price.

rules.text: Layer into a stock with several strikes rather than going all in at one strike.
Prefer puts below the lower Bollinger Band.
For a $100K account a high-priced stock like COR ties up too much per put, so use a smaller ETF.

steps.does: States the cap on exposure per stock when layering puts.
steps.why: Limit risk of assignment in any one name; smaller for higher P/E names.
data: no more than 10% of portfolio in AAT
about 5% in BE because of higher P/E
steps.conclusion: Room for one or two more AAT puts.

rules.text: Keep a higher P/E stock like BE to about 5% of the portfolio.

tools.name: Unidentified brokerage app
tools.used_for: account overview, realized gain/loss and open put positions

indicators.name: 50-day moving average
indicators.how_used: share of stocks above it for breadth; pullback target on single stocks

indicators.name: 20-day moving average
indicators.how_used: listed with other averages and VWAP for GLW

indicators.name: Bollinger Bands
indicators.how_used: mid band as support target, puts below lower band, upper band hug means pullback likely

indicators.how_used: yearly VWAP as a level to eye for put strikes

indicators.name: P/E ratio
indicators.how_used: GLW 71 versus 120 earlier; BE high so keep size small

indicators.name: Call wall
indicators.measures: strike with large call gamma, resistance

indicators.name: Put wall
indicators.measures: strike with large put gamma, support

indicators.name: Position size
indicators.measures: share of portfolio in a name
